articles.title: In Hakeem Jeffries’ Rise to Speaker, Black Leaders See a Milestone—and a Test
articles.summary: In 1870, Joseph Rainey of South Carolina became the first Black person to serve in the U.S. House. This week, current and newly elected House Democrats are poised to meet to select Rep. Hakeem Jeffries as the chamber’s first Black Speaker. It is a moment fraught with meaning and hurdles for both the New York Democrat and the larger Black community, multiple Black leaders tell TIME. articles.title: Trump’s Golf Course Plans Hit a Legal Obstacle: His Own Social Media Posts
articles.summary: President Donald Trump faced a legal setback on Saturday when a federal judge temporarily blocked the planned closure of a public golf course and surrounding parkland in Washington, D.C. Among the evidence undermining his Administration’s justification: his own Truth Social posts. articles.title: All Hail Philomena Cunk, the Perfect Fake Newswoman for Our Age of Ignorance
articles.summary: In the future, when some documentary series in whatever medium succeeds television looks back at the current decade in public discourse, it might name our era the Age of Ignorance. The crank shouting nonsense from atop a soapbox is, of course, nothing new. What’s unique to our time is how vast the audiences for these bloviators have become. articles.title: Air Traffic Control Systems Are Outdated. What’s Being Done to Prevent Another Outage?
articles.summary: Transportation Secretary Sean Duffy on Saturday blamed the previous day’s nationwide ground stop on the replacement of copper wires at a “remote” Federal Aviation Administration (FAA) facility. Installing new fiber optic lines led to critical communication breakdowns, he said. About 7,500 flights were delayed and over 9,000 were canceled on Friday, according to FlightAware . articles.title: The China Shock in the AI Era
articles.summary: Americans are anxious about artificial intelligence . In the midterm elections , they voted to slow down its expansion. Forty local ballot measures in 10 states promise to tighten restrictions on data-center construction, with overwhelming public support. Measures to limit development of data centers won more than 70% of the vote in 30 of these electoral contests.
